executiveSummary: TallChairAdvisor.com has a severe CTR extraction problem: 101,257 impressions yielding only 275 clicks (0.27% CTR) across 20 audited pages. The dominant issue is AIO suppression on informational queries (knee-pain, correct-dimensions) where CTR is structurally unrecoverable via snippet rewrites. On commercial/review pages where the SERP is escapable, the primary levers are schema correctness (itemReviewed missing on all Review-typed blocks, @id gaps), a cluster of spec-accuracy errors on the Leap Plus seat-height configuration, title-length violations, and an unresolved first-person voice breach on a non-Gesture page. Affiliate tag compliance and internal-linking into money pages are secondary but in-scope revenue levers per the Profit Audit directive.
weeklyFocus: 1. Fix the Leap Plus seat depth spec error in /review/leap-plus/ meta and body copy (15.75"–19.75" → 15.75"–18.75") — this is a factual error on the #1 money page (14,090 impr, 43 clicks) that actively misleads buyers and is the highest-severity deterministic defect on the site.

2. Add itemReviewed to Review schema nodes on /review/aeron-size-c/ and /review/leap-plus/, and add Product @id to /review/leap-plus/ — these are carried-over CRITICAL/HIGH schema fixes that block rich result eligibility on the two money pages with the most commercial impression volume (18,838 combined impressions).

3. Build the email capture opt-in on /knee-pain-seat-depth/ (ConvertKit, Seat Depth Checklist PDF) — this is Thesis Step 1, still unbuilt, and is the only revenue lever available on the site's highest-impression page (40,581 impr) where organic CTR is structurally AIO-suppressed and unrecoverable via any snippet rewrite.

findings.summary: Meta description publishes a seat depth spec of '15.75"–19.75"' that does not match the verified Steelcase specification (15.75"–18.75" per the Steelcase Seating Specification Guide), inflating the maximum by 1 inch and misleading buyers.
findings.recommendation: Correct the meta description to: 'Research-based spec analysis for tall users 6'0"–6'6". Seat depth 15.75"–18.75", 500 lb capacity, 19.5" seat height standard (22.5" with optional 5" cylinder).' (151 chars). Also audit the page body for any recurrence of the 19.75" seat depth figure and replace with 18.75".
findings.evidence: Meta desc states: 'Seat depth 15.75"–19.75"'. Verified spec (decisions-log 2026-08-06): standard seat depth 15.75"–18.75". The review/gesture/ page correctly states 18.75". Leap Plus seat HEIGHT (not depth) has a 19.5" standard max. The two specs appear cross-contaminated.

findings.summary: Page title and meta description publish the standard seat height floor as 15.5" when the verified spec is 15.5"–19.5" standard — the floor figure itself is correct but the title label omits 'Standard' context that is essential given the optional cylinder configuration, creating misleading framing.
findings.recommendation: Verify page body does not present 15.5" as the floor when the optional cylinder is in use — the floor shifts to 17.5". Meta is technically correct; ensure body copy makes the configuration dependency explicit: 'Standard cylinder: 15.5"–19.5". Optional 5" cylinder (+~$63): 17.5"–22.5" — the floor rises, not just the ceiling.' This is a carried-over critical spec issue from decisions-log 2026-08-06 affecting 28 pages.
findings.evidence: Title: 'Steelcase Leap Plus Seat Height: 15.5"–19.5" Standard'. Decisions-log 2026-08-06 confirms standard cylinder is 15.5"–19.5" and optional 5" cylinder is 17.5"–22.5" — the floor RISES with the optional cylinder (17.5", not 15.5"). Meta states 'Steelcase Leap Plus seat height is 15.5"–19.5" standard, or 17.5"–22.5" with the optional 5" cylinder' — this is correct. However, top queries include 'leap size' and 'is the steelcase leap for heavy people?' indicating intent mismatch; the page ranks for Leap v2 queries. 511 impr, 0 clicks, pos 8.8.
